analyst.summary: NALCO posted a record FY26 PAT of Rs 5,816cr (+10.4% YoY), but the underlying story is two different commodity spikes in two different years: FY25's back-half profit was an alumina-price windfall (spot alumina hit $650-695/t, since crashed to ~$305-310/t), while FY26's rebuild was an LME-aluminium windfall (aluminium spiked to $3,685/t in April 2026 on China's 45mt smelter cap plus Middle East supply disruptions, still $3,100-3,200/t in mid-July). PE of ~11.2x looks undemanding on paper, but on a cycle-adjusted view -- normalizing aluminium down and letting depressed alumina partially recover -- normalized earnings power looks meaningfully lower than the TTM print, putting the 'true' multiple closer to 13-15x. The growth pipeline (Pottangi bauxite mine, ~3.5 MTPA; Angul smelter + 1,080MW power JV, ~Rs 30,000cr capex) is real and debt-free-funded but FY2029-30 dated, so it does not help the next 3 years. Balance sheet quality (zero debt, ROE 26.8%, ROCE 36.6%), a ~2.9% dividend yield, and no confirmed government OFS overhang (promoter holding 51.3%, near the practical floor for divestment) support holding an existing position; but with the stock already up 95.5% over 12 months and two independent brokerages both at Neutral, this reads as fair value, not a bargain.
